You had noodles with fried spring rolls, not “Pho Beef with spring roll” as what you have claimed and the official name for your dish is “Bun Cha Gio" as what we all here call it in Vietnam.

For “Bun Cha Gio”, it is a dry dish and there’s spicy fish sauce that comes with it in a separate small bowl. You should pour it into your main bowl and it's up to your liking on how much sauce you want to add into your main bowl – and that’s how you eat it. We would greatly appreciate if you have asked us about it in the first place.

As what we have replied to similar queries on our alleged “pricey” meals; overpriced meals are very subjective especially when there are choices between dining out in the open-air hawker streets (meals start from VND30, 000) and enjoying the comfort of modern clean set-up air-conditioned indoor restaurant equipped with free WiFi along with other essentials of self-indulgence (meals start from VND70, 000). The choice is yours.

For those who unfamiliar with restaurants’ standard practice (but not all practicing it), there’s a menu stand at the entrance displaying the range of meals and dishes along with the respective price tags for potential customers to browse through. And before you decide to dine in at the restaurant, again the choice is yours.

Apparently, all prices stated on our menu are tax-inclusive. We didn't surprise you with other hidden charges/costs. And thus, we believed that you knew what you were paying for.
